faq.q: Should I make a square or a vertical version?
faq.a: Vertical 9:16 fills the screen in Stories and Reels, and square 1:1 sits neatly in the feed. You can make one of each. Every version is its own run, with the cost shown before it starts.

faq.q: Can I make a promo before my product photos are ready?
faq.a: You can start from a text description alone, but the product won't match your real one. For an ad, wait until you have a clear photo of the final item so shoppers see what they'll actually get.

faq.q: What length should a launch promo use?
faq.a: Use 6 seconds for a quick reveal, 10 or 15 seconds for a product action, and 30 seconds when the launch needs a full product story. Choose 9:16 for vertical channels.

faq.q: Which ratio is best for launch day?
faq.a: Use 9:16 for TikTok and Reels, and a 1:1 version for feeds and listings. Both come from the same source photo.

faq.q: Can I make teaser content before stock arrives?
faq.a: Yes. Use a clear product photo to make a coming-soon clip, and add the date as editable text.

faq.q: What does a launch clip cost?
faq.a: A 6-, 10-, 15- or 30-second clip costs 24, 40, 60 or 120 credits, shown before the job starts.

faq.q: What belongs in a launch teaser?
faq.a: Show the product and the reveal, then add the planned date as editable text so the teaser can be updated.

faq.q: How is a teaser different from release-day creative?
faq.a: A teaser can say coming soon; release-day creative should show the live date, current offer, and the product link.

faq.q: Where should I put the launch discount?
faq.a: Add the approved price or discount as an editable layer in a clear area after download and verify it on a phone preview.

faq.q: What should I check before publishing?
faq.a: Confirm the product shape, launch date, price, stock status, link, and crop in the final post.

faq.q: Can I have launch ads ready before the product is in stock?
faq.a: Yes. Use a clear photo of the final item to make a coming-soon teaser and add the date as editable text. Wait for a confirmed release date before advertising an exact delivery promise.

faq.q: Do I need a creator or a studio to film the launch?
faq.a: No. One photo of the final product becomes a creator-led review, unboxing or demo clip for a fixed credit cost shown up front. The people on screen are AI-generated, so present the clip as your own ad, not as a customer review.
